item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 022308
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Wed Sep 2 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Karina, located well east of the Hawaiian Islands, on Hurricane
Lowell, located several hundred miles south of the Hawaiian Islands,
and on Tropical Storm Marie, located several hundred miles
south-southwest of the southern tip of the Baja California
Peninsula.

Offshore of Southwestern Mexico:
An area of low pressure could form well offshore of southwestern
Mexico over the weekend or early next week. Gradual development is
possible during the early to middle part of next week as the system
moves west-northwestward at 10 to 15 mph, and is likely to remain
well offshore of Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

$$
Forecaster Evans/Hagen

--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 PM HST (0300 UTC), the center of Hurricane Karina was located 
near latitude 19.3 North, longitude 134.7 West. Karina is moving 
toward the west-northwest near 10 mph (17 km/h) and a 
west-northwestward motion is expected over the next few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 130 mph (215 km/h) with higher 
gusts.  Karina is a category 4 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson 
Hurricane Wind Scale.  A slow weakening trend is forecast the next 
few days, followed by a more steady rate of weakening. Karina is 
likely to remain a hurricane the next couple of days.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 35 miles (55 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125 miles
(205 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 947 mb (27.97 inches).

item.title: Hurricane Karina Forecast Discussion Number 27
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Wed Sep 02 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 030239
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Karina Discussion Number  27
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP112026
500 PM HST Wed Sep 02 2026

Latest infrared satellite imagery of Karina suggests that convective 
cloud-top temperatures continue to warm. Karina continues to 
maintain an annular appearance, while the eye remains cloud-filled. 
The latest TAFB subjective Dvorak intensity estimate held steady 
from 18z to 00z, at 5.5/6.5 or 127 kt. Objective intensity estimates 
from CIMSS vary around 105-110 kt. Given the warming cloud-top 
temperatures over the last several hours, the initial intensity 
estimate was adjusted down slightly to 115 kt. 

Karina is currently moving west-northwestward around 9 kt. A 
subtropical ridge to the north of Karina should cause the cyclone to 
continue moving west-northwestward for the next couple of days.  
Karina is then expected to turn more northwesterly later this week 
as the subtropical ridge is weakened by an oncoming upper-level 
trough.  Karina's track forecast was nudged slightly to the east of 
the previous forecast, reflecting a blend of HCCA and GDMI. Models 
exhibit relatively strong agreement in Karina's track through the 
first 48 h, before spread increases thereafter.

While vertical wind shear is expected to remain very weak over the 
next 48 h, Karina is expected to track toward cooler SSTs and into 
a drier mid-level environment. The latest NHC intensity forecast 
shows a slightly faster rate of weakening than the previous 
forecast, but still lies at the high end of the guidance envelope 
for the first 3 days, and then closer to the intensity consensus 
at days 4 and 5. The hostile environmental conditions should 
cause Karina to lose its convection and become post-tropical by 
day 5.

PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 300 DEGREES AT 10 MPH...17 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...985 MB...29.09 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 PM MST (0300 UTC), the center of Hurricane Marie was located 
near latitude 18.4 North, longitude 113.1 West. Marie is moving 
toward the west-northwest near 10 mph (17 km/h). This motion should 
continue through tonight followed by a turn more west-northwestward 
for the next several days.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 80 mph (130 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Additional strengthening is forecast through 
Friday. Gradual weakening is anticipated to begin by this weekend.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 40 miles (65 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 185 miles
(295 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 985 mb (29.09 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Marie will affect portions of the coast of
southwest Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula for the next few
days and will likely spread northward to southern California over
the weekend.  These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf
and rip current conditions. Please consult products from your local
weather office. A depiction of rip current risk for the United
States can be found at:
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?ripCurrents
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 AM MST.
 
$$

item.title: Hurricane Marie Forecast Discussion Number 8
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM MST Wed Sep 02 2026 
581 
WTPZ43 KNHC 030247
TCDEP3
 
Hurricane Marie Discussion Number   8
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP132026
800 PM MST Wed Sep 02 2026
 
The latest infrared satellite imagery shows a burst of convection is 
attempting to wrap around the center of Marie. This is a moderate 
amount of improvement over the last several hours, as the hurricane 
seems to have shaken off the dry air seen earlier. The most recent 
TAFB subjective Dvorak fix is T4.5/77 kt and the UW-CIMSS objective 
intensity estimates are in the range of 62-75 kt. Based on the 
given data for this advisory, the initial intensity has been set to 
70 kt making Marie a hurricane. 

The general motion for Marie is to the northwest at 320/10 kt, and 
the cyclone is expected to maintain that heading for the next 
several days as a narrow mid-level ridge located to the north will 
steer the hurricane off to the west-northwest. During this time, the 
cyclone should slow down as the ridge gradually weakens. There is 
still a good amount of cross-track spread that is due to how much an 
amplified mid-latitude trough, off the western United States coast, 
erodes the previously mentioned ridge. The current NHC track is 
similar to the previous track but slightly farther south. This track 
is still a bit north of the HCCA track. 

The intensity for this forecast is a little higher than the previous 
forecast. Given that the hurricane is expected to continue to be in 
favorable conditions with sea-surface temperatures (SSTs), diagnosed 
by the SHIPS guidance between 27-29 C, relative humidity around 70 
percent, and light wind shear, Marie is likely to continue to 
intensify. The peak forecast is tricky in this situation due to the 
potential for Marie to move over the cold wake left by Iselle last 
week, as these waters may cap the peak intensity. Marie should be 
crossing the 26 C SST isotherm after 60 h, and weakening is expected 
to begin in earnest beyond this time period.
